title: Sonographic examination of implants to differentiate between peri-implant health, mucositis and peri-implantitis. Prospective 3-year cohort study of patients with implants and removable superstructures
summary: The reason for conducting the study is to investigate a diagnostic measure to differentiate between peri-implant health, mucositis and peri-implantitis on dental implants with removable superstructures. This is done with the help of ultrasound measurement, which is a non-invasive, cost-effective, painless and radiation-free method for visualizing hard and soft tissue on teeth and implants. As part of the clinical routine treatment, the teeth and implants are examined clinically and radiologically. In addition to the routine treatment, ultrasound measurements are taken on the teeth and implants; a period of 10 minutes is allowed for this. If the dynamic assessment of the degree of inflammation and quantification of tissue perfusion in sonographic images leads to a differentiation between peri-implant health, mucositis and peri-implantitis, ultrasound measurement can be used in routine dental diagnost.

interventions.name: In the study, 30 patients from the Department of Orofacial Prosthetics and Functional Dentistry at the Medical Center for Dental, Oral and Maxillofacial Medicine in Marburg/Lahn were examined. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age 30-80 years (male or female)   
- treated periodontal disease (stage I-III with grade A-C).  
- Non-smoker  
- no caries  
- Patients must be able to clean their teeth independently
- Lower and upper jaw with sufficient bone for implants  
- Implant sites must be free of infection and root fragments
 - Written declaration of consent
Exclusion criteria:
- systemic diseases (e.g. untreated diabetes mellitus, osteoporosis, Parkinson's disease)    
- mental disability that may impair the participant's ability to follow study instructions
- Diseases of the oral mucosa (e.g. pemphigus)    
- Long-term medication with steroids, bisphosphonates    
- Known allergic reactions to dental materials    
- Malignant tumor in the head and neck area    
- Requirement of concurrent radiotherapy or chemotherapy or radiotherapy or chemotherapy within the last 10 years    
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding at the start of the study  
- Abuse of drugs, alcohol and medication  
- Current orthodontic treatment
